## Why visit

A food-led choice that still has a legitimate cask reason to visit. The restored former Boddington’s pub and its modern dining extension offer a different experience from the smaller surviving locals. Its best use is as a deliberate meal stop on a Salford circuit rather than a destination for maximum beer variety. The published British menus, Sunday service and advance-order sharing pies give you concrete options for making one pub visit a substantial food experience as well.

## Beer

CAMRA documents two cask handpumps, usually with local beer; check which are operating on the day.

## Cider and perry

**Real-cider offering not established.** No current real-cider evidence established; ask for the producer and product at the bar.

See [how cider is classified](../real-cider.md).

## Food

Pub classics, modern British dishes and Sunday roasts. Sharing pies require pre-order; check the current booking terms.

## Plan the visit

Reserve for a meal and distinguish the pub menu from the restaurant menu. Cask range is limited compared with New Oxford.

**Getting there:** Walk from Salford Central; combine with New Oxford, Kings Arms and Eagle Inn.

Check [November transport issues](../logistics.md) for date-specific disruption.
